Half-point lower rate, or $50K less borrowed? Milton buyers, here is the monthly math.

Example only, computed with Canadian semi-annual compounding, 25-year amortization:
1) $600,000 at 4.44% = about $3,301 a month.
2) $600,000 at 3.94% (half a point lower) = about $3,137 a month, saving about $164.
3) $550,000 at 4.44% ($50,000 less borrowed) = about $3,026 a month, saving about $275.
The 4.44% example is the lowest 5-year fixed rate published by Ratehub.ca on Nov 6, 2026; 3.94% is a hypothetical. Lenders also apply the stress test and debt ratios, so what you qualify for may differ.

Want help working out your own budget? Comment INFO to get full details, or call 905-452-4298.

Example only. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

Voiceover: AI-generated in Krishna's own voice.

Krishna Rander, Realtor® | PROPERTY.CA INC., Brokerage

#miltonontario #mortgagemath #firsttimehomebuyer #keyswithkrishna

frames.say: Milton buyers: lower rate or less borrowed?
First, a six hundred thousand dollar mortgage at four point four four percent is about thirty-three hundred dollars a month.
Next, a half-point lower rate brings it to about thirty-one hundred thirty-seven dollars. That saves one hundred sixty-four dollars a month.
Finally, borrowing fifty thousand dollars less brings it to about three thousand twenty-six dollars. That saves two hundred seventy-five dollars a month.
So all in, borrowing fifty thousand dollars less saves about two hundred seventy-five dollars a month, versus one hundred sixty-four dollars from a half-point lower rate.

caption:
Jobs fell. Will the Bank of Canada hike again on Dec. 9?

The Canadian Press (via BNN Bloomberg, Nov 6, 2026) reports Canada lost 4,700 jobs in October and the unemployment rate rose two tenths to 6.7%. The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate a quarter point to 2.5% on Oct. 28. As of Nov 6, LSEG put the odds of another quarter-point hike at the Dec. 9 decision at 35%. CIBC's Andrew Grantham says that if oil and labour softness persist, CIBC forecasts the Bank will hold in December.

Example only: a quarter-point change (4.44% to 4.69%, 25-year amortization, semi-annual compounding) is about $14 a month per $100,000 borrowed. Variable rates follow the Bank's rate; fixed rates follow bond yields.

Hike or hold on Dec. 9? Comment your guess.

Want help planning your budget? Comment INFO to get full details, or call 905-452-4298.

Forecasts can change. Not financial or mortgage advice. Sources: The Canadian Press / BNN Bloomberg, Nov 6, 2026; Ratehub.ca, Nov 6, 2026.
